Each D has its own critical solution. Over one echo period its centre field p1 is a wave: here it is swept from D 38 to 232.6 through the stored solutions.
Scaled by √(D−2) the waves nearly coincide. Across D the solution is close to one shape, shrunk by 1/√(D−2).
3. Inside one wave, each harmonic is a fixed factor smaller
Built harmonic by harmonic, the wave at D 38 converges by a steady factor per term. On a log scale the harmonics fall on near-straight lines, steeper at higher D.
4. The wave is the slope of a surface at the centre
A solution is a field p over the radius x and the echo phase θ. Near the centre p ≈ p1 x, so p1 is the slope of this surface at x = 0.
